prompt: A mux has more data inputs than before, but the designer leaves too few binary select codes to name them all. What is the problem?

options.text: Some inputs will automatically be ORed together
options.explanation: A mux selects an input; it does not merge unnamed inputs.
Data width and selection-code width are separate.

options.text: A decoder will recover the missing address information
options.explanation: A decoder cannot create distinct choices from identical select codes.

options.text: Not every input can be selected independently
options.explanation: Correct. Each selectable input needs its own selection code.

workedExample: Selection lines name the input to forward. If two inputs have no distinct codes, the mux cannot choose between them independently. Adding a select bit doubles the available codes; it does not add a bit to the data value.

prompt: A three-input function is high on rows 1, 2, 6 and 7, using binary order A, B, C. A and B select a four-way mux, with A as the high select bit. What should data inputs I0, I1, I2, I3 receive?

options.explanation: This plugs in constants as if F were a function of A and B only. F depends on C within the AB = 00 and AB = 01 rows.
This reverses both the C polarities and the last two inputs: rows m4, m5 (AB = 10) are 0, and m6, m7 (AB = 11) are 1.
Correct. For each AB, look at the two rows C low and C high: 00 → (0, 1) = C; 01 → (1, 0) = C'; 10 → (0, 0) = 0; 11 → (1, 1) = 1.

options.text: It needs an 8-to-1 mux; a 4-to-1 mux cannot implement a 3-input function
options.explanation: A 4-to-1 mux can implement any 3-input function. In general, a mux whose select lines take all but one of the inputs can implement any function of them, by feeding the last variable, its complement or constants into the data inputs.

workedExample: For each fixed AB pair, inspect the two C cases. With AB at 00 the outputs are zero then one, so copy C. At 01 they are one then zero, so invert C. At 10 both are zero; at 11 both are one. Connect those four behaviours to the corresponding mux inputs. The mux selects a small function of the remaining input, not just a constant.
